answer: Topology-Bandwidth Gate. An agent earns outbound bandwidth only through verified neighbor relays: its inlet to the wider network is capped by the count of distinct nodes that have independently routed traffic through it. Because each new identity must first be bridged into the relay mesh by existing nodes, an attacker must convince many distinct honest relays to carry its traffic before it gains reach. Isolated clusters therefore spiral inward, starved of bandwidth, and each forged identity costs the attacker real relay capacity plus sustained forwarding work.
